subject: Audit exports: staged streaming vs on-demand handoff
messages:

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — NorthRiver is working through a SOC 2 readiness checklist and we need concrete options for how Redwood can deliver admin activity evidence. We also need an example manifest and schema to run by our internal auditors.

Hi Elise —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise runbook that covers (1) what we capture, (2) retention tiers, and (3) delivery/export options with operational notes. I also attached an export spec (export_spec_v1.pdf) and a short sample manifest (audit_sample_manifest.csv).

1) WHAT WE LOG (admin & audit surface)
- Authentication events: successful/failed logins, SSO assertions, MFA events (timestamp, actor, source IP, auth method).
- Authorization changes: role grants/revokes, policy updates, group membership changes.
- Privileged operations: key import/rotation, KMS bindings, credential uploads, service-account changes.
- Model serving admin: model uploads, model pin/version changes, rollout/canary events, instance scaling decisions.
- API-level events: user-facing API calls (authenticated caller id, endpoint, request id), admin API calls (create/delete/config changes).
- KV/prefix cache operations (when configured): cache invalidation, cache warming events (metadata only, not payload).
- System actions: node reboots, orchestration actions, failover triggers (operational telemetry).

Note: We do not store customer input payloads in admin logs by default; API request metadata (request id, model id, token counts, requester id) is logged for traceability. PII redaction is available as a post-processing step for bundled exports.

2) RETENTION TIERS (default + add-ons)
- Default (Hosted): 30 days of full-fidelity admin logs (searchable via Console).
- Extended: 90 days — available as a paid add-on for Dedicated and Enterprise customers.
- Archive: 1 year (compressed, immutable snapshots) — for customers with longer legal/contractual needs; retention beyond 1 year by special arrangement.
- Legal hold: customer-initiated hold can preserve specific slices (by tenant id/timebox) indefinitely until release.

3) DELIVERY / EXPORT OPTIONS
A) On-demand bundle (recommended for audits)
  - What: Point-in-time tarball containing newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) admin events, signed manifest (HMAC-SHA256) and a JSONL schema.
  - How: Delivered as an encrypted S3 presigned URL or pushed to the customer's SFTP endpoint. We support AES-256-GCM encryption for payloads; keys can be customer-managed (Bring-Your-Own-KMS) or Redwood-managed.
  - Integrity: Signed manifest + SHA256 checksums for each file. Optional notarization (attestation) available for SLA-backed handoffs.
  - When to use: SOC 2 evidence bundles, auditor requests, legal eDiscovery.

B) Continuous streaming (best for near-real-time monitoring)
  - What: Streaming export of admin events to a customer endpoint (Kafka, Kinesis, or HTTPS delivery) in NDJSON with a stable schema and sequence tokens.
  - Security: Mutual TLS for delivery endpoints + per-record sig (HMAC) option. Transport-level TLS required; we recommend mTLS for Kafka/Kinesis connectors.
  - Schema & dedupe: Events include sequence_id + checkpoint tokens to support incremental reconciliation. Redundancy & at-least-once semantics are standard; we include monotonic offsets for replay.
  - When to use: Continuous SIEM ingest, real-time alerting, automated compliance checks.

C) Incremental delta snapshots
  - What: Periodic (hourly/daily) delta bundles that contain only changes since last snapshot, useful to reduce transfer size.
  - When to use: Large tenants, cost-sensitive archival where full continuous stream is not required.

4) DATA PROTECTION & CHAIN OF CUSTODY
- Encryption at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Optional BYOK via customer KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) for export encryption keys.
- Signed manifests with HMAC-SHA256 and optional public attestation for high-assurance handoffs.
- Immutable manifests and checksums to support auditor verification.

5) OPERATIONAL NOTES & SLAs
- On-demand bundles: typical lead time 24–48 hours for standard requests; expedited delivery (same-day) available as a paid option.
- Streaming connectors: onboarding workshop + connector validation (2–5 business days).
- Sample retention of download URLs: presigned links expire after 7 days by default.

Attachments: audit_sample_manifest.csv (example manifest) and export_spec_v1.pdf (delivery schema + field definitions).

If you want, we can run a 60-minute readiness session (joint security + infra) to pick the right pattern for your auditors. Proposed agenda: scope, schema walk-through, KMS choices, delivery endpoint test.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Elise — quick follow to call out pricing/SLA choices and procurement steps so your legal team can review earlier:

- Standard audit bundle (30d retention): included in Hosted Enterprise subscription (no extra fee) for up to 1TB of export data per year.
- Extended retention (90d): add-on at $X/month (per-tenant).
- Continuous streaming connector: one-time onboarding fee + $Y/month per connector for throughput and monitoring.
- Expedited on-demand export (same-day): one-time service fee; SOW applies for recurring same-day commitments.

Procurement / next steps:
- If NR wants BYOK for export objects we need: KMS ARN, key policy approval, and a test key.
- For streaming, provide a non-prod endpoint for validation; we will run a 48-hour smoke test.
- Execute an NDA amendment for attestation notarization (if required).

I can loop legal/procurement on a short email once you confirm the delivery pattern.

—Kimberly
